talk.title: Sales Copilot: Turn complex technical inquiries into clear, accurate offers in minutes, not hours!
talk.abstract:
Sales CoPilot as a solution that helps teams turn complex technical customer inquiries into clear, accurate quotations much faster, reducing turnaround from hours to minutes.

The business problem: technical sales requests are slow, difficult, and error-prone when handled manually.

The Solution: Our Sales CoPilot interprets complex requirements, works with documentation and technical data, and supports offer preparation.

Technology foundation: strong emphasis on AWS as the enabler, plus AI/LLM-driven processing. Architecture choice: a set of core AWS services to deliver both the user-facing application and the AI-powered data processing pipeline. Amazon S3 stores uploaded product datasheets and hosts the frontend assets, while Amazon CloudFront accelerates and securely delivers the web interface to users. Incoming application traffic is routed through an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to containerized services running on Amazon ECS, which handle both backend business logic and document ingestion tasks. For AI capabilities, Amazon Bedrock is used in two places: to extract and transform structured information from PDF datasheets, and to power the agentic logic behind the application. Persistent structured data is stored in Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, which supports read/write operations from the backend. Together, these AWS services provide a scalable, cloud-native architecture for hosting, processing, AI enrichment, and application delivery.

talk.title: Beyond Vibe Coding
talk.abstract:
AI agents are changing how engineers write, test, and ship code. This talk explores what agentic coding looks like in practice - the workflow, the tradeoffs, and the tools that make it work.

We'll cover how to collaborate effectively with AI agents: prompting, reviewing, iterating, and knowing when to take over. We'll look at what changes when development gets significantly faster - testing strategies, CI/CD pipelines, and team coordination all need to keep up. Then we'll introduce Kiro, an agentic IDE that uses spec-driven development, steering rules, and hooks to let engineers define how the agent operates within their codebase. We'll also look at AWS DevOps Agent - an autonomous operations teammate that correlates metrics, logs, and deployment history to investigate incidents and identify root causes before you even open your laptop.

speakers.name: Sergio Lopez-Gehler
speakers.bio: Sergio is a Solutions Architect at AWS, based in Vienna, Austria. He brings a strong background in Data Engineering, Data Science, and Machine Learning. Since the emergence of LLMs, he has been deep in the trenches building applications that leverage this technology — from RAG pipelines to agentic flows and everything in between. Before making the jump to tech, he spent years in academia as a physicist, working across Astronomy and Particle Physics.
